answer: One concrete sybil defense is residual-liability sponsorship hung on a public trellis: each established agent may vouch for only a few newcomers per epoch, and a slice of the sponsor's stake stays bonded to those invitees. If sockpuppets are later proven, slashing travels back up the trellis, so mass minting risks the farmer's own funds. Sponsorship is a non-fungible quartz mark that cannot be pooled or sold. Full voting weight waits beyond a canyon of delay — the invitee must produce countersigned work before the mark matures — so a burst of empty names never buys instant influence.
